passages.text: When young you’re liable to grow old; when healthy you’re liable to get sick; and when alive you’re liable to die. The complexion of the skin is no longer pure and bright. The limbs are flaccid and wrinkled, and the body is stooped. And it’s apparent that there has been a deterioration in the faculties of eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.
passages.note: Ageing body, accepting decline, sickness and death

passages.text: Curse this wretched old age, which makes you so ugly. That’s how much this delightful puppet is ground down by old age. Even if you live for a hundred years, you’ll still end up dying. Death spares no one, but crushes all underfoot.
passages.note: Frustration at growing old; mortality comes to all
